learn.title: How Wind Turbines Generate Electricity
learn.intro: Wind turbines are key to the clean energy transition, converting moving air into electricity without emissions. Understanding how they work helps us appreciate their role in reducing fossil fuel dependence and powering homes sustainably.
learn.c1_text: Wind turbine blades are shaped like airplane wings, creating lift as wind flows over them. This lift causes the blades to spin, turning a shaft connected to a generator. A typical modern turbine converts about 40-50% of wind energy into electricity.
learn.c2_text: Inside the nacelle, the spinning shaft drives a generator that uses magnetic fields to convert rotational energy into electrical energy. Most turbines use either synchronous or asynchronous generators, producing alternating current (AC) suitable for the power grid.
learn.c3_text: India ranks 4th globally in wind capacity with over 40 GW installed by 2023. The country's wind-rich states like Tamil Nadu and Gujarat lead in deployment, contributing significantly to India's renewable energy targets of 500 GW by 2030.
learn.stat1: A typical wind turbine can power 600 homes annually
learn.stat2: Modern turbines capture 40-50% of wind energy as electricity
learn.stat3: India's installed wind capacity reached 40 GW by 2023
learn.stat4: Turbine rotor diameters can span up to 160 meters

learn.title: Small Wind Turbines for Homes and Communities
learn.intro: Small wind turbines offer decentralized energy solutions for rural and suburban areas, reducing grid dependence and providing clean power where large turbines aren't feasible. They're vital for community resilience and local energy independence.
learn.c1_text: Small wind turbines are typically under 100 kW, designed for residential, agricultural, or small commercial use. Unlike utility-scale turbines, they're installed closer to where electricity is consumed, often on rooftops or short towers.
learn.c2_text: Effective small wind systems require consistent wind speeds above 9 mph (4 m/s). Proper tower height is crucial—usually 30 feet above obstacles—to access stronger, steadier winds. Zoning regulations vary widely across jurisdictions.
learn.c3_text: India's Ministry of New and Renewable Energy promotes small wind systems for remote villages. The Sewa RAM program supports distributed wind-diesel hybrid systems, aiming to electrify off-grid communities through the Deendayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana scheme.
learn.stat1: Small turbines are typically under 100 kW capacity
learn.stat2: Effective systems need minimum 9 mph (4 m/s) average wind speed
learn.stat3: Tower height should be 30 feet above local obstacles
learn.stat4: India targets 60 GW wind capacity by 2030 including small systems

learn.title: Rooftop Solar and Net Metering in India
learn.intro: Rooftop solar paired with net metering policies enables Indian households and businesses to become prosumers, selling excess power back to the grid. This democratizes energy production and accelerates India's clean energy transition.
learn.c1_text: Rooftop solar panels convert sunlight directly into DC electricity using photovoltaic cells. An inverter changes DC to AC for home use. Excess power flows to the grid, while net meters track energy exchange, crediting consumers for surplus generation.
learn.c2_text: Net metering allows consumers to offset electricity bills by exporting surplus solar power to the grid at retail rates. India's central government issued guidelines in 2022, but state-level implementation varies, with some states offering better tariff structures than others.
learn.c3_text: India launched the Grid Connected Rooftop Solar Programme with INR 240 billion budget. States like Gujarat and Rajasthan lead in installations. The government aims for 40 GW rooftop solar capacity by 2022, with net metering policies implemented across major states.
learn.stat1: India targets 40 GW rooftop solar capacity by 2022
learn.stat2: Net metering credits surplus power at retail electricity rates
learn.stat3: Grid-connected systems can reduce electricity bills by 70-90%
learn.stat4: Over 15 Indian states have implemented net metering regulations

learn.title: Second Life EV Batteries for Grid Storage
learn.intro: EV batteries retain 70-80% capacity after retirement from vehicles, making them valuable for stationary energy storage. Repurposing these batteries reduces waste and provides cost-effective grid storage solutions for renewable integration.
learn.c1_text: EV batteries typically last 8-10 years in vehicles before dropping below 70-80% capacity. While insufficient for automotive range requirements, this remaining capacity is ideal for stationary applications like home energy storage or grid support services.
learn.c2_text: Repurposed EV batteries provide frequency regulation, peak shaving, and renewable energy smoothing. These applications don't require full capacity—typically needing only 20-40% of original performance. Systems can be modular, scaling from residential to utility scale.
learn.c3_text: India's EV market is rapidly expanding under FAME schemes. With over 2 million EVs on roads by 2023, second-life battery potential is significant. NITI Aayog estimates India could have 14 GWh of retired EV batteries annually by 2030 for reuse.
learn.stat1: EV batteries retain 70-80% capacity after vehicle use
learn.stat2: Retired batteries can serve 8-15 years in stationary storage
learn.stat3: India could generate 14 GWh of used EV batteries annually by 2030
learn.stat4: Second-life batteries cost 30-50% less than new storage systems

learn.title: Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) Technology
learn.intro: Vehicle-to-grid technology transforms electric vehicles into mobile energy assets that can stabilize the power grid during peak demand or supply fluctuations. This bidirectional energy flow maximizes EV value beyond transportation.
learn.c1_text: V2G-enabled EVs can both draw power from and supply power back to the grid using bidirectional chargers. A typical EV battery (60 kWh) can supply 5-10 kW of power, enough to support several households during peak demand periods.
learn.c2_text: V2G fleets provide frequency regulation, voltage support, and peak load management. Aggregated EV batteries respond within seconds to grid signals, offering faster response times than traditional power plants. This improves grid reliability and accommodates variable renewables.
learn.c3_text: India's first V2G pilot was launched by CESL in 2022 with Tata Motors. The government's National Electric Mobility Mission Plan supports smart charging infrastructure. With 2 million+ EVs projected by 2030, V2G could provide significant grid flexibility services.
learn.stat1: A 60 kWh EV battery can supply 5-10 kW of grid power
learn.stat2: V2G fleets respond to grid signals within seconds
learn.stat3: India projects 2 million EVs on roads by 2030
learn.stat4: V2G can provide 10-15% additional grid capacity during peaks

learn.title: Solar Panel Types Comparison
learn.intro: Different solar panel technologies offer varying efficiencies, costs, and applications. Choosing the right type affects system performance and return on investment, making it crucial for optimizing solar installations in diverse environments.
learn.c1_text: Monocrystalline panels use single silicon crystals, achieving 20-22% efficiency. Polycrystalline panels use melted silicon fragments, offering 15-17% efficiency. Monocrystalline performs better in low light but costs 20-30% more per panel.
learn.c2_text: Thin-film panels use materials like amorphous silicon or cadmium telluride, applied in thin layers. They're lightweight, flexible, and perform well in high temperatures. However, they require more space with only 10-12% efficiency compared to crystalline panels.
learn.c3_text: India's Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme allocates INR 19,500 crore for solar manufacturing. The government targets 20 GW domestic module production capacity. This reduces import dependency, currently at 85%, supporting local thin-film and crystalline silicon manufacturing.
learn.stat2: Polycrystalline panels offer 15-17% efficiency at lower cost
learn.stat3: Thin-film panels provide 10-12% efficiency with flexibility benefits
learn.stat4: India imports 85% of solar modules despite PLI scheme
